s: A healthcare company stores AWS Backup recovery points for Amazon EBS, Amazon RDS, and Amazon EFS in a dedicated backup account. After a ransomware incident at a peer company, the CISO requires that no one can delete recovery points or shorten their retention before 35 days. This includes the root user of the backup account and administrators of the organization's management account. The protection itself must be impossible to remove once it is in force. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Apply AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode to the vault with a minimum retention of 35 days, and let the grace time expire so the lock becomes immutable.
Apply AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode to the vault with a minimum retention of 35 days, and restrict the backup:DeleteBackupVaultLockConfiguration permission to a break-glass role.
Attach an SCP to the backup account that denies backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint and backup:UpdateRecoveryPointLifecycle for all principals.
Configure the backup vault to store recovery points in an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 35-day default retention.

w.y: After its grace time ends, Vault Lock in compliance mode cannot be changed or deleted by anyone, including the root user or AWS. Recovery points cannot be deleted before the minimum retention. Only compliance mode satisfies 'impossible to remove' and 'including root'.

o.A: Correct: compliance-mode Vault Lock becomes immutable after the grace time and enforces the minimum retention.
o.B: Governance mode can be removed by any principal that has the right IAM permissions, so it is not immutable.
o.C: Management account administrators can detach or change SCPs, and SCPs never restrict the management account itself.
o.D: AWS Backup stores recovery points in its own managed storage, not in a customer S3 bucket you can Object Lock.

d: impossible to remove once in force (including root)
